'''Krzysztof Sacha''' (born September 2, 1970) is a Polish [[theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]]. He is currently Professor of Physics at the [[Jagiellonian University]] in Cracow.<ref>{{cite web | title=Krzysztof Sacha | url= https://chaos.if.uj.edu.pl/~sacha | publisher=Department of Physics, JU | year=2021 | access-date=2021-09-02}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Krzysztof Sacha was born on September 2, 1970, in [[Kłodzko]] together with his twin brother Jerzy Sacha. In 1996 he married Ewa, with whom he has two children Aleksandra and Wojciech.

==Education==
He received a Master of Science in Physics in 1995 and a Ph.D. in Physics in 1998, both with distinction, from Jagiellonian University. 
In 1999 he was given Award of Ministry of Polish Education for PhD thesis. He continued his work in Jagiellonian University, in 1999-2000 in Philipps University Marburg with Fellowship of the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation, and in 2005-2006 in Los Alamos National Laboratory with Fulbright Fellowship. In 2004 he earned [[Habilitation]] in physics in Jagiellonian University and in 2011 he was awarded title of  Professor of Physics.<ref>{{cite web | title=Professorship nominations February 24 2011 | url= https://www.prezydent.pl/archiwum-bronislawa-komorowskiego/aktualnosci/nominacje/art,672,prezydent-wreczyl-nominacje-profesorskie.html| publisher=The official website of the President of the Republic of Poland | year=2021 | access-date=2021-09-02}}</ref>

==Research==
Krzysztof Sacha researches atomic physics. He is known for his work on [[Bose–Einstein condensate]] fluctuations, solitons, Eckhardt-Sacha model of nonsequential triple ionization,<ref>{{cite journal| title=Three-electron correlations in strong laser field ionization |last1=Efimov|first1= Dmitry K.|last2=Maksymov|first2=Artur|last3=Ciappina|first3=Marcelo|last4=Prauzner-Bechcicki|first4=Jakub S.|last5=Lewenstein|author-link5=Maciej Lewenstein|first5=Maciej|last6=Zakrzewski|first6=Jakub|journal=Optics Express |year=2021 |volume=29 |issue=17 |pages=26526–26537 |doi=10.1364/OE.431572 |pmid=34615086 |arxiv=2104.14438 |bibcode=2021OExpr..2926526E |s2cid=233444323 |url=https://www.osapublishing.org/oe/fulltext.cfm?uri=oe-29-17-26526&id=453973}}</ref> first proposal of [[Spontaneous symmetry breaking|symmetry breaking]] of discrete time translation symmetry - [[Time crystal]]s<ref>{{cite news|newspaper=Polish Press Agency|title=Dyskretny urok kryształów czasu zbadał także Polak|url=https://naukawpolsce.pap.pl/aktualnosci/news,413528,dyskretny-urok-krysztalow-czasu-zbadal-takze-polak.html|access-date=2021-10-23}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | title=A Brief History of Time Crystals|last1=Khemani|first1=Vedika| last2=Moessner | first2=Roderich|last3=Sondhi| first3=S. L. | year=2019 |arxiv=1910.10745 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book | title=Time Crystals (SSAOPP, volume 114) | series= Springer Series on Atomic, Optical, and Plasma Physics| url= https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007%2F978-3-030-52523-1| publisher=Springer | year=2021 | volume= 114| doi= 10.1007/978-3-030-52523-1| isbn= 978-3-030-52522-4| s2cid= 240770955| access-date=2021-09-02}}</ref> and many other works on dynamical [[Phase (matter)|phases of matter]]<ref>{{cite news |title=Prof. Sacha z UJ: Ścigamy się z Google'em o kryształ czasowy. I mamy przewagę|newspaper = Gazeta Wyborcza |url=https://wyborcza.pl/7,75400,27696331,jak-odkrywalismy-krysztaly-czasowe-polscy-fizycy-scigaja-sie.html| access-date = 2021-10-23}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=Krzysztof Sacha's Google Scholar profile | url= https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=vXJ40DoAAAAJ| year=2021 | access-date=2021-09-02}}</ref>
==Recognition==
In 2024, Sacha received the [[Prize of the Foundation for Polish Science]] in the field of [[mathematics]], [[physics]], and [[engineering]] for his works on for the formulation of the theory of time crystals.<ref>https://naukawpolsce.pl/aktualnosci/news%2C105163%2Cprof-krzysztof-sacha-laureatem-nagrody-fnp.html</ref>
